You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test case `testCodec112` calls the method `Base64.encodeBase64(byte[] in, boolean isChunked, boolean urlSafe, int maxResultSize)` with parameters including `isChunked=false` and a `maxResultSize` parameter equal to the output array length from a previous encodeBase64 call.

Examining the method `Base64.encodeBase64(byte[], boolean, boolean, int)`, it first computes the length of the encoded Base64 output using a helper method `getEncodeLength`. This computed length is compared against the provided `maxResultSize`, and if the computed length exceeds `maxResultSize`, an IllegalArgumentException (IAE) is thrown.

The key detail is that `getEncodeLength` calculates the output length based on three parameters: the input byte array, a chunk size, and a chunk separator length. The method computes the length assuming chunking is applied (adds chunk separators if chunk size > 0). It increases the expected output length by the length of the chunk separator depending on how the length aligns with chunk boundaries.

Back in the main method, whether `isChunked` is true or false determines which Base64 instance constructor is used. However, in the early length check, the `getEncodeLength` uses a constant chunk size `MIME_CHUNK_SIZE` and the standard chunk separator bytes regardless of the `isChunked` flag.

Hence, if `isChunked` is false (no chunking), the length estimation incorrectly adds chunk separator lengths, making the computed length greater than the actual output length. This causes the check `if (len > maxResultSize)` to fail and throw an IllegalArgumentException even when the actual encoded output will fit in the provided `maxResultSize`.

The test triggers this bug by setting `isChunked=false` but passing the output length from a prior encoding (which was non-chunked and thus shorter). The code mistakenly treats the effective length with chunking even though chunking is disabled, triggering the erroneous exception.

In summary, the length calculation does not properly consider if chunking is enabled when estimating the output length, leading to false detection that output size exceeds maxResultSize when chunking is false.

This matches the current bug report description that the method throws IAE for valid maxResultSize when `isChunked=false`.

Recent bug reports about base64 encoding size issues seem analogous but do not provide additional direct insight.

The root cause is in the length calculation and checks in `encodeBase64(byte[], boolean, boolean, int)`, specifically how chunking is considered or ignored when estimating output length.

The fix should adjust the call to `getEncodeLength` to either pass 0 chunk size and/or empty chunk separator bytes when `isChunked` is false so length calculation reflects non-chunked output length and prevents incorrect exceptions.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test calls Base64.encodeBase64(byte[], boolean isChunked, boolean urlSafe, int maxResultSize) with isChunked=false but maxResultSize set to the output length of a prior encodeBase64 call without chunking. The encodeBase64 method calculates the required output length by invoking getEncodeLength with constant chunk size and chunk separator bytes which assume chunking is enabled. This results in an overestimation of the output length as chunk separator lengths are added even when chunking is disabled. Consequently, the check if (len > maxResultSize) throws IllegalArgumentException incorrectly, as the calculated length is larger than maxResultSize even though the actual output fits. The bug arises from not adjusting the chunk size and chunk separator passed to getEncodeLength based on the isChunked flag. This explains why valid maxResultSize values cause exceptions with isChunked=false. The solution is to modify encodeBase64 to pass 0 chunk size and empty separator bytes when isChunked is false, correctly estimating the non-chunked output size and avoiding erroneous exceptions.

Suggested methods for fix:
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64.encodeBase64(byte[],boolean,boolean,int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
